clips.text_zh: 我個CFD今日又輸，因為美債息向上突破，2年、10年、30年全部升緊 basis points。FED話cut息又反悔，依家仲話要 unprice it。Term premium狂升，我嘅long全部被打爆。又係學費 thx 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Bonds, bonds, bonds — watch the screen. Two-year, ten-year, and thirty-year yields are all going up. Basis points keep rising, higher and higher. The Fed said it would cut rates, then reversed. Now markets are trying to unprice that cut. Term premium is spiking, and anyone long on bonds got wrecked today.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about bond yields breaking out and the Fed cutting then unpricing it

signal.rationale: Macro rates observation, no actionable setup

clips.text_en_b2: Bonds are absolutely hammered today because yields across the curve, from two-year all the way through thirty-year, have broken out in a serious way. The Fed hinted at rate cuts, then walked it back, and now markets are scrambling to unprice those expectations entirely. Term premium is spiking aggressively, which means anyone brave enough to be long got absolutely wrecked on their CFD positions. Cheap tuition once again, thanks market 🙏
clips.text_en_c1: Bond yields have staged a coordinated breakout across the entire curve, with two-year, ten-year, and thirty-year paper each climbing several basis points within the session. The Federal Reserve, which had previously signalled a forthcoming rate cut, appears to have walked back that guidance, prompting markets to unprice the anticipated easing. Term premium has expanded sharply as a result, and anyone running long-duration positions has effectively been steamrolled. My own CFD book caught the brunt of it, which is precisely the sort of expensive tuition one keeps paying. The takeaway is that policy reversals remain the most reliable source of drawdown when leverage is in play.
clips.text_en_c2: Bond yields have staged a coordinated breakout across the curve, with two-, ten-, and thirty-year Treasuries all grinding higher in basis points. After the Federal Reserve hinted at imminent rate cuts only to backtrack, money markets are now scrambling to unprice the dovish assumption they had previously baked in. Term premium, that elusive compensation for duration risk, is spiking sharply, punishing anyone foolish enough to remain long. My CFD book got thoroughly eviscerated — every position bled out in sympathy. Each rout is, I suppose, tuition paid in full to the bond market's unflinching pedagogy, though the syllabus remains stubbornly opaque. Patience, then, and an open mind for the next session.

clips.text_zh: TSLA同Musk嘅新聞又出。佢公開呼籲美國同中國嘅AI Lab要合作 lol，仲話「America must team up with China」。Hyperscaler邊個唔緊張？NVDA同TSMC點算？觀望先 🤔
clips.text_en_b1: Elon Musk just announced that America must team up with China on AI. The Semafor article quotes Musk calling for cooperation between US and China AI labs. This hits TSLA, NVDA, and the whole semiconductor supply chain. Chip stocks are already volatile on the news.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread about Musk calling for US-China AI lab cooperation

signal.rationale: Musk US-China AI cooperation headline adds uncertainty to semis, no clear directional setup

clips.text_en_b2: Elon Musk has publicly come out and stated that America must team up with China on AI development, a pretty bold call given the current geopolitical climate. Semafor quoted him urging direct cooperation between US and Chinese AI labs. That sort of framing inevitably rattles the hyperscalers, and NVDA, TSMC, and the broader semiconductor supply chain are all feeling the heat. Chip stocks were already volatile, so right now, just watching how this plays out 🤔
clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk has once again thrust himself into the geopolitical spotlight by publicly advocating that American AI laboratories should collaborate directly with their Chinese counterparts. The remarks, which a Semafor piece attributes to Musk himself, carry the somewhat provocative headline that America must team up with China. Such rhetoric inevitably unsettles hyperscalers and the broader semiconductor value chain, since NVDA and TSMC investors are particularly sensitive to any whiff of policy ambiguity. Chip equities, which had already been volatile amid export-control chatter, slid on the news. For now I am sitting on my hands and watching how the narrative develops before committing fresh capital.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk has once again commandeered the headlines, this time publicly advocating a strategic rapprochement between American and Chinese artificial-intelligence laboratories. His assertion that 'America must team up with China,' as reported by Semafor, lands like a grenade in the hyperscaler ecosystem. Nvidia, TSMC, and the entire semiconductor value chain must now grapple with the geopolitical implications of such a partnership, however speculative. Chip equities have grown conspicuously jittery, oscillating on every nuance emanating from Musk's prolific commentary. Tesla itself remains tethered to the founder's every pronouncement. For the moment, prudence dictates observation rather than commitment — the fog of speculation is simply too dense to penetrate.

clips.text_zh: AI agent 即將取代工程師嘅節奏越來越快 🤖 Anthropic 出咗份聲明，話自己 operating income 有正數，但要撇除 model training 成本同 Amazon revenue sharing。如果唔計 AI infra 燒錢，根本唔可能 profit。睇住先，靠AI續命中。
clips.text_en_b1: Anthropic says it is profitable, but only if you ignore model training costs and revenue sharing with partners like Amazon. Investors were reassured that adjusted operating income will stay positive for one more quarter. Gross margins are above 80% before those costs. This came up on /g/ today.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread about Anthropic claiming profitability while ignoring training costs

signal.rationale: AI industry observation, not a trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Anthropic has put out a statement claiming profitability, although the figure only holds up once you strip out model training costs and the revenue-sharing arrangement with Amazon. Adjusted operating income is expected to remain positive for another quarter, and gross margins sit above eighty percent before those expenses are factored in. Strip the AI infrastructure burn out of the equation though, and the whole profit narrative more or less falls apart. Definitely worth keeping an eye on 🤖
clips.text_en_c1: Anthropic has circulated a statement asserting that its operating income has turned positive, though the claim hinges on figures that exclude the considerable cost of model training and the revenue-sharing arrangements it maintains with partners such as Amazon. Strip those line items out, and the underlying economics arguably look rather less flattering, given how lavishly capital is being deployed on AI infrastructure. Investors appear to have taken some comfort from the assurance that adjusted operating income will remain in the black for at least another quarter, and gross margins comfortably exceed eighty per cent before those exclusions. The whole exercise does feel a touch like creative accounting.
clips.text_en_c2: Anthropic has circulated a statement professing profitability, though the headline figure warrants the closest scrutiny. Once one excludes the colossal expenditure on model training alongside revenue-sharing obligations to partners such as Amazon, the ostensibly rosy adjusted operating-income metric becomes considerably less flattering. Gross margins admittedly exceed eighty percent before these deductions, yet the underlying economics of frontier AI remain overwhelmingly capital-intensive. Investors, evidently desperate for a narrative of sustainability, seized upon the announcement as confirmation that Anthropic can remain cash-flow positive for at least another quarter. The discourse on technical forums has predictably dissected the sleight of hand. One suspects the company is, quite literally, living on borrowed inference.

clips.text_zh: Hong Kong news time：美國首次公開承認喺太空部署咗武器 🇺🇸🚀 中國同俄羅斯已經回應，局勢升溫。SpaceX Starlink會唔會變軍事目標？幾年後返Florida嘅我覺得呢單嘢要留意。
clips.text_en_b1: The US has confirmed for the first time that it deployed weapons in space. China and Russia have already responded. SpaceX Starlink could become a military target. The news comes from CBS, and Asia markets are watching the escalation closely this week.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread about US confirming weapons in space and China/Russia reacting

signal.rationale: Geopolitical news observation, not a trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: The United States has officially confirmed, for the first time ever, that it has deployed weapons in space, a move that has already drawn sharp responses from both China and Russia. Tension is clearly escalating, and there is growing chatter about whether SpaceX Starlink could end up being treated as a legitimate military target. CBS broke the story, and Asian markets are watching developments closely this week, given how much infrastructure now sits up there 🇺🇸🚀
clips.text_en_c1: The United States has, for the first time on the record, formally acknowledged that it has deployed weapons in space, a development that Beijing and Moscow have already moved to condemn. Observers are now debating whether the constellation of SpaceX Starlink satellites, which has thus far enjoyed a quasi-civilian status, might henceforth be treated as a legitimate military target. The confirmation, which originated with CBS, has injected a fresh dose of geopolitical risk into a region whose supply chains were already stretched thin. Asian markets, ever sensitive to such escalations, appear to be pricing in the possibility of further volatility in the sessions ahead.
clips.text_en_c2: The United States has, for the first time on the public record, formally acknowledged the deployment of weapons in outer space — a disclosure of considerable strategic consequence. Beijing and Moscow have already issued pointed responses, and the diplomatic temperature is rising in lockstep with the orbital escalation. Whether SpaceX's Starlink constellation, ostensibly civilian, may now be construed as a legitimate military target is the question consuming analysts from Hong Kong to Washington. CBS carried the original reporting, and Asian bourses opened the week under a pall of geopolitical uncertainty. The trajectory of this confrontation, one fears, will define the security architecture of the coming decade.

clips.text_zh: 睇咗個post，有人一個月冇deadlift，返到 gym 即刻舉到 220kg 做兩下，PR 係 240kg。我條腰就廢 😂 肥仔信話佢又想雞髀ladder，佢今日叫我地9點gym。Conviction 高到我已經set咗鬧鐘。
clips.text_en_b1: I went deadlifting again after a month off. I did 220 kg for a double and probably could have done more reps. My PR is 240 kg and I have gotten stronger since. Next session I should try 245 or 250 kg. I trained at home with kettlebell clean and press in between.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread about deadlifting 220kg for a double after training at home

signal.rationale: Fitness progress post, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: After roughly a month away from deadlifts, I jumped straight back in and managed 220 kilograms for a double, which honestly felt like I had plenty left in the tank. My previous PR sits at 240, although I have gotten noticeably stronger since then, so next session I should probably push for 245 or even 250. In between gym days I trained at home with kettlebell clean and press to keep things moving. Conviction is high, alarm already set 😂
clips.text_en_c1: After roughly a month away from the platform, I returned to the gym and pulled a clean double at 220 kilograms, with several repetitions still left in reserve had I chosen to chase them. My all-time personal record stands at 240, set before the layoff, and I am quietly convinced that I have since grown stronger still, which suggests a credible case for attempting 245 or even 250 next session. In the interim I have been training at home with kettlebell cleans and overhead presses, exercises that seem to have preserved, if not enhanced, my posterior-chain recruitment. Progress, it seems, does occasionally survive a brief hiatus.
clips.text_en_c2: After an entire month away from the bar, I returned to the platform and promptly hoisted 220 kilograms for a clean double, with at least another repetition evidently still in the tank. My longstanding personal record sits at 240 kilograms, set months ago, though subsequent training cycles suggest I have since grown measurably stronger. The next session ought to feature an audacious attempt at 245, perhaps even 250, should the bracing hold and the lumbar spine deign to cooperate. In the interim, kettlebell clean-and-press at home has served as tolerable maintenance work. Conviction in the programme remains, for now, thoroughly undiminished, however emphatically my lower back may protest.

clips.text_zh: 下工返屋企煲劇，今晚想睇返舊番。有人post Hellsing、Wolf's Rain、Bleach、Azumanga Daioh 全部都係2000年代神作。我自己最近想睇返 Gundam 00，搭嗰陣 FE 溫書溫到癲 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Seasonal anime is fine, but it is often more fun to go back and rewatch older stuff. Lately on /a/ people are posting Hellsing, Wolf's Rain, Bleach, and Azumanga Daioh. These 2000s shows still hold up today. Classic anime is better than most new releases.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread about rewatching 2000s anime like Hellsing and Bleach

signal.rationale: Anime culture discussion, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Seasonal anime tends to be solid, but honestly there is something far more satisfying about going back and revisiting older gems. Lately /a/ has been flooded with recommendations for Hellsing, Wolf's Rain, Bleach, and Azumanga Daioh, all proper 2000s classics. They have aged remarkably well and honestly still hold up against most modern releases. I am personally leaning towards rewatching Gundam 00, since I used to study engineering while binging it 🧐
clips.text_en_c1: Contemporary seasonal anime has its merits, yet there is something undeniably satisfying about revisiting the catalogue of titles that defined the medium two decades ago. Lately, threads across the board have been championing Hellsing, Wolf's Rain, Bleach, and Azumanga Daioh, each of which remains remarkably rewatchable despite the inevitable march of production techniques. For my part, I find myself gravitating towards Gundam 00, a series I recall studiously avoiding during the frantic exam revision period that once consumed my evenings. Whether nostalgia is the operative factor or simply a preference for tighter plotting, the classics of that era hold up with admirable resilience.
clips.text_en_c2: Contemporary seasonal offerings, while occasionally arresting, seldom possess the peculiar staying power of the medium's earlier vintage — which is precisely why a rewatch feels increasingly warranted after the working day concludes. Lately, aficionados on the relevant boards have been championing Hellsing's gothic bombast, Wolf's Rain's melancholic world-building, Bleach's shonen verve, and Azumanga Daioh's quiet absurdism, all canonical artefacts of the 2000s. These productions, despite their years, remain remarkably resilient against the caprice of taste. Personally, I find myself drawn back toward Gundam 00, whose mecha-political texture I had once consumed while grinding through examinations. The classics, one concedes, endure.

clips.text_zh: 今日跟 Tommy 去 site 做 underground utilities condition survey，搵 CCTV crawler 影地下渠管，有兩段 pipe wall 好薄。返寫字樓要寫 GI report 入落 factor of safety check。考牌溫書又少咗兩粒鐘，靠AI續命 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: I spent today on a drainage condition survey for underground utilities. Two pipe sections have very thin walls and need to be flagged in the GI report. The factor of safety calculation depends on the pipe class and bedding condition. Site work is slow but useful for the FE exam.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about responsible adult financial planning borrowed for engineering grind context

signal.rationale: Professional work observation, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: I spent the whole day on site with Tommy running a condition survey of underground utilities, sending a CCTV crawler through the drains to capture the interior of two pipe sections. Both ended up showing pretty thin pipe walls, which I will definitely have to flag in the GI report once I get back to the office. The factor of safety calculation ultimately hinges on pipe class and bedding conditions. Two fewer hours of FE revision tonight 🙏
clips.text_en_c1: I spent the better part of today accompanying him on site, where we conducted a condition survey of underground utilities using a CCTV crawler to inspect the buried drainage runs. Two of the pipe segments we examined exhibited wall thicknesses that were, frankly, alarmingly thin and will need to be flagged prominently within the forthcoming GI report. Back at the office, the data must now be reconciled with the factor-of-safety calculation, which itself depends on the pipe class and the prevailing bedding conditions observed during the inspection. Two more hours of FE revision have consequently slipped away, sacrificed to professional obligations.
clips.text_en_c2: Today found me accompanying Tommy to site for an underground utilities condition survey, deploying a CCTV crawler through subterranean conduits to capture a comprehensive visual record. Two segments of pipework betrayed wall thicknesses so attenuated as to warrant immediate flagging in the forthcoming GI report — a document that will subsequently feed into the factor-of-safety calculation, contingent upon pipe classification and the prevailing bedding conditions. The fieldwork, although methodical and unhurried, consumed hours that my FE revision schedule could scarcely spare. Artificial intelligence tutoring tools must, regrettably, absorb the resultant deficit. Such is the perennial arithmetic of a junior engineer's professional education — perpetual motion between trench and textbook.
